taxonomyNote: Some authors (Duellman et al. 2016) place it in Hyliola; NatureServe notes Banker et al. (2020) argued against that and that Hyliola has not been widely adopted. The USGS fact sheet calls it the 'California chorus frog'.
fieldMarks: Gray or light brown with small dark brown spots; rough skin; white belly with yellowish limbs and groin.
Adults 2.5-5.1 cm snout-vent length; toe pads are large and wide, with webbing.
Baja California treefrog more often has a dark eye stripe, is more often green and has smaller toe pads; males of this species have a dusky yellow throat.
Call is a repeated pattern of fast, loud, low-pitched quacks; tadpoles have eyes inside the outline of the head.
behavior: Mostly nocturnal except in the breeding season, when it may call day and night; breeds about February-early October.
By day retreats to shaded rock crevices near the waterline; most movements are under 25 m.
Eats insects, spiders and centipedes as adults; lays eggs singly, attached to twigs or loose on the bottom.
Aestivates in extreme heat or cold; inactive in cold or hot, dry weather.
habitat: Rocky canyons near streams and washes with permanent pools, from desert and coastal stream courses to mountain pine belt.
Requires some shade; breeds in quiet water of rocky streams.
range: Southwestern California south into northern Baja California, Mexico, from near sea level to about 2,290 m. Not found in Canada.
